prerequisites: Prior knowledge of the subject Graphic Expression from the first year is recommended.
Students should have notions of sketching, fluent handling of drawing software, and skill in bibliographic consultation.

learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand and apply technological and graphic concepts adapted to new situations for professional development.
Develop strategies and procedures in solving graphic problems as a way to approach engineering projects.
Use graphic communication among technicians, specifically in creating and interpreting standardized Industrial Engineering Technical Drawing plans, incorporating new technologies.
Work in teams, where they can develop their knowledge with a critical and responsible technical/cultural exchange.
Plan and manage projects in the field of industrial engineering according to current legislation.
Interpret and represent assembly and detail drawings of mechanisms, structures, and installations.
Master and fluently use parametric drawing programs.
Determine operating conditions of common parts in mechanisms and the relationship between them.
Correctly use specifications, regulations, and mandatory graphical representation standards.
Know how to create virtual models of engineering installations.

syllabus_topics: Module 1: Parametric modeling of mechanical elements
Installation, environment and project management in Autodesk Inventor.
Design assistants I: shafts, keys, bearings, pins.
Design assistants II: gears, springs, belts and chains.
Other environments: Welding, Sheet metal parts.
Shafts and axles, keys and pins.
Other transmission elements: belts and chains.

assessment_methods.method: Active participation in expositive classes (theory) and laboratory practices (EV4)

assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation, students must attend at least 80% of practical classes (both PA and PL); otherwise, they will be considered as 'not presented'. The final grade is calculated as 0.2*EV1 + 0.3*EV2 + 0.3*EV3 + 0.2*EV4. If the minimums are not reached, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. EV1 and EV2 require a minimum of 50% of their maximum score to be passed. Grades for passed evaluation systems are maintained until the extraordinary evaluation, but not for the next academic year. Students who do not complete the group work may defend an individual assignment in the extraordinary evaluation. In extraordinary evaluation, students must retake theoretical and/or practical exams (EV1 and EV2). If group work (EV3) was not completed or passed, an individual assignment will be provided by professors. Students under differentiated evaluation will be assessed solely on EV1 (40%) and EV2 (60%).
